## Warm-up{.smaller}

Let's talk about sampling distributions.  

## Motivation for today{.smaller}

As a consultant + masters/PhD adviser ...

... one of the first things I routinely get asked is to conduct a power analysis

So let's learn this together!

We are going to learn this in the difference in means context. This extends to difference in proportions, etc. etc. 

## Warm-up{.smaller} 

A company wants to determine whether two types of pens differ in their average writing time (measured in minutes before running out of ink). A random sample of 35 blue-ink pens and 40 black-ink pens is selected. The number of minutes each pen writes before running out of ink is recorded. You can assume that both sample standard deviations are 8-minutes for each pen.

Is there sufficient evidence to conclude that the mean writing time differs between blue-ink and black-ink pens?

Set up our null and alternative hypothesis: 

$H_o:$

$H_a:$

## Warm-up{.smaller} 

$H_o: \mu_b = \mu_{bk}$

$H_a: \mu_b \neq \mu_{bk}$

-- How do we make decisions/conclusions in fixed level testing?

## Errors 

|                       | $H_o$ is True | $H_o$ is False |
|-----------------------|---------------|----------------|
| Reject $H_o$          | ____________  | ____________ |
| Fail to Reject $H_o$  | ____________  | _____________ |

## Errors 

$H_o: \mu_b = \mu_{bk}$

$H_a: \mu_b \neq \mu_{bk}$

-- What would be a Type-1 Error in the context of this problem?

-- What would be a Type-2 Error in the context of this problem?

## Context 

Suppose we calculated the following

p-value ~ 0.321 vs $\alpha = 0.05$

Does this mean we **did** make a Type-1 Error?

## Context 

Suppose we calculated the following

p-value ~ 0.321 vs $\alpha = 0.05$

Does this mean we **did** makea Type-1 Error?

**NO** 

## Type-1 Error 

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

alpha <- 0.05
z_crit <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)

data <- data.frame(x = seq(-4, 4, length.out = 1000))
data$y <- dnorm(data$x)

ggplot(data, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_area(
    data = subset(data, x <= -z_crit),
    fill = "steelblue",
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_area(
    data = subset(data, x >= z_crit),
    fill = "steelblue",
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = c(-z_crit, z_crit),
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "red"
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = -2.5, y = 0.03, label = expression(alpha/2),
           color = "steelblue", size = 5) +
  annotate("text", x = 2.5, y = 0.03, label = expression(alpha/2),
           color = "steelblue", size = 5) +
  labs(
    title = "Sampling Distribution Under the Null Hypothesis",
    x = "Test Statistic",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Questions 

## Type-2 

What would be a Type-2 Error in the context of this problem?

Fail to reject the null hypothesis that $\mu_b = \mu_{bk}$ when $\mu_b = \mu_{bk}$ is actually false (we should have rejected)!

In order to calculate this probability (and power), we need to make an assumption on what $\mu_b - \mu_{bk}$ actually is!

Let's assume that $\mu_b - \mu_{bk} = 5$. 

## Why 5?{.smaller}

The true difference of 5 minutes is an assumed **effect size** for the purpose of calculating the probability of a Type II error. It is not something we know from the sample data.

Effect size is a quantitative measure of the magnitude of a difference, relationship, or effect in a population.

We might choose 5 because...

1. Previous research: Earlier studies may suggest that one type of pen lasts approximately 5 minutes longer than the other.

2. Practical significance: The company might consider a 5-minute difference large enough to matter when deciding which pen to manufacture or sell.

In practice, we may calculate the probability of a Type-2 error for many many different effect sizes!

## The plot{.smaller}

I want to just give us time to think, ask questions, and explain what's going on.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(ggplot2)

alpha <- 0.05
effect_size <- 5
se <- 1.852

crit <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2) * se

x <- seq(-6, 11, length.out = 2000)

null <- data.frame(
  x = x,
  y = dnorm(x, mean = 0, sd = se)
)

alternative <- data.frame(
  x = x,
  y = dnorm(x, mean = effect_size, sd = se)
)

beta <- pnorm(crit, mean = effect_size, sd = se) -
        pnorm(-crit, mean = effect_size, sd = se)

ggplot() +
  # Type I error: two tails under the null distribution
  geom_area(
    data = subset(null, x <= -crit),
    aes(x = x, y = y, fill = "Type I Error (alpha)"),
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_area(
    data = subset(null, x >= crit),
    aes(x = x, y = y, fill = "Type I Error (alpha)"),
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  # Type II error: central region under the alternative distribution
  geom_area(
    data = subset(alternative, x >= -crit & x <= crit),
    aes(x = x, y = y, fill = "Type II Error (beta)"),
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  # Null and alternative distributions
  geom_line(
    data = null,
    aes(x = x, y = y, color = "Null Distribution"),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = alternative,
    aes(x = x, y = y, color = "Alternative Distribution"),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  # Critical values
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = c(-crit, crit),
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "black"
  ) +
  # Type I error labels
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = -4.8, y = 0.025,
    label = "alpha/2",
    parse = TRUE,
    size = 4
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 4.5, y = 0.025,
    label = "alpha/2",
    parse = TRUE,
    size = 4
  ) +
  # Type II error label
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 0, y = 0.035,
    label = paste0("beta = ", round(beta, 2)),
    color = "darkorange3",
    size = 4
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Error Regions",
    values = c(
      "Type I Error (alpha)" = "steelblue",
      "Type II Error (beta)" = "orange"
    )
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Sampling Distributions",
    values = c(
      "Null Distribution" = "steelblue4",
      "Alternative Distribution" = "darkgreen"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Sampling Distributions of the Difference in Means",
    subtitle = "Two-sided test with alpha = 0.05 and a true difference of 5 minutes",
    x = "Difference in Sample Means (minutes)",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-6, 11)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# How do we calculate this?

## Things we need to know 

-- We need to propose an effect size $\mu_b - \mu_{bk}$ ✅ 

-- Calculate the standard error 

-- Calculate the critical values (at what value or "more extreme" we would reject)

## Standard error 

Please solve!

$SE=\sqrt{\frac{s_1^2}{n_1}+\frac{s_2^2}{n_2}}$

## Standard error 

$SE=\sqrt{\frac{8^2}{35}+\frac{8^2}{40}}=1.852$

## Things we need to know 

-- We need to propose an effect size $\mu_b - \mu_{bk}$ ✅ 

-- Calculate the standard error ✅ 

-- Calculate the critical values (at what value or "more extreme" we would reject)

## Critical values

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(ggplot2)

alpha <- 0.05
effect_size <- 5
se <- 1.852

crit <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2) * se

x <- seq(-6, 11, length.out = 2000)

null <- data.frame(
  x = x,
  y = dnorm(x, mean = 0, sd = se)
)

alternative <- data.frame(
  x = x,
  y = dnorm(x, mean = effect_size, sd = se)
)

beta <- pnorm(crit, mean = effect_size, sd = se) -
        pnorm(-crit, mean = effect_size, sd = se)

ggplot() +
  # Type I error: two tails under the null distribution
  geom_area(
    data = subset(null, x <= -crit),
    aes(x = x, y = y, fill = "Type I Error (alpha)"),
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_area(
    data = subset(null, x >= crit),
    aes(x = x, y = y, fill = "Type I Error (alpha)"),
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  # Type II error: central region under the alternative distribution
  geom_area(
    data = subset(alternative, x >= -crit & x <= crit),
    aes(x = x, y = y, fill = "Type II Error (beta)"),
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  # Null and alternative distributions
  geom_line(
    data = null,
    aes(x = x, y = y, color = "Null Distribution"),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = alternative,
    aes(x = x, y = y, color = "Alternative Distribution"),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  # Critical values
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = c(-crit, crit),
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "black"
  ) +
  # Type I error labels
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = -4.8, y = 0.025,
    label = "alpha/2",
    parse = TRUE,
    size = 4
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 4.5, y = 0.025,
    label = "alpha/2",
    parse = TRUE,
    size = 4
  ) +
  # Type II error label
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 0, y = 0.035,
    label = paste0("beta = ", round(beta, 2)),
    color = "darkorange3",
    size = 4
  ) +
  # Arrows pointing to the critical values
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = -4.7, y = 0.245,
    label = "Critical value",
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  annotate(
    "segment",
    x = -4.0, y = 0.225,
    xend = -crit, yend = 0.12,
    arrow = grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(0.15, "cm")),
    color = "black"
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 5.0, y = 0.245,
    label = "Critical value",
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  annotate(
    "segment",
    x = 4.4, y = 0.225,
    xend = crit, yend = 0.15,
    arrow = grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(0.15, "cm")),
    color = "black"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Error Regions",
    values = c(
      "Type I Error (alpha)" = "steelblue",
      "Type II Error (beta)" = "orange"
    )
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Sampling Distributions",
    values = c(
      "Null Distribution" = "steelblue4",
      "Alternative Distribution" = "darkgreen"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Sampling Distributions of the Difference in Means",
    subtitle = "Two-sided test with alpha = 0.05 and a true difference of 5 minutes",
    x = "Difference in Sample Means (minutes)",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-6, 11), ylim = c(0, 0.28)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Critical values 

For this example, we are going to use 2.032 for our $t^*$. 

The critical values are then... 

1.852 * 2.032 = 3.76

1.852 * (-2.032) = -3.76

## Type II Error 

Therefore, we calculate the probability that the observed difference in sample means falls between the critical values, assuming the true difference is 5 minutes.

$\beta=P(-3.76<\bar{x}_1-\bar{x}_2<3.76)$

## Type II Error 

$$
\begin{aligned}
\beta
&=P\left(\frac{-3.76-5}{1.852}<t<\frac{3.76-5}{1.852}\right)\\
&=P(-4.72<t<-0.67)\\
&=\Phi(-0.67)-\Phi(-4.72)\\
&=0.2536-0.0000 (\text{very small number})\\
&\approx 0.2536
\end{aligned}
$$
$\Phi$ represents the cumulative probability up to that point on the distribution.

## Type II Error 

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(ggplot2)

df <- 34

ggplot(data.frame(x = c(-5, 4)), aes(x)) +
  stat_function(fun = dt, args = list(df = df)) +
  
  # Phi(-4.72)
  stat_function(
    fun = dt,
    args = list(df = df),
    geom = "area",
    xlim = c(-5, -4.72),
    alpha = 0.3
  ) +
  
  # Phi(-0.67)
  stat_function(
    fun = dt,
    args = list(df = df),
    geom = "area",
    xlim = c(-5, -0.67),
    alpha = 0.15
  ) +
  
  geom_vline(xintercept = -4.72, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = -0.67, linetype = "dashed") +
  
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = -2.5,
    y = 0.08,
    label = "25%",
    size = 6
  ) +
  
  labs(
    x = "t",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Type II Error 

In R

```{webr-r}
pt(-0.67, 34, lower.tail = T) - pt(-4.72, 34, lower.tail = T)
```

# Questions 

# Power 

## Power 

Power is the probability that a hypothesis test correctly rejects $H_o$ when $H_o$ is false.

|                       | $H_o$ is True | $H_o$ is False |
|-----------------------|---------------|----------------|
| Reject $H_o$          | ____________  | Power |
| Fail to Reject $H_o$  | ____________  | _____________ |

And Power is a good thing!

## Power 

The green area is power. How do we suppose power is calculated?

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(ggplot2)

alpha <- 0.05
effect_size <- 5
se <- 1.852

crit <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2) * se

x <- seq(-6, 11, length.out = 2000)

null <- data.frame(
  x = x,
  y = dnorm(x, mean = 0, sd = se)
)

alternative <- data.frame(
  x = x,
  y = dnorm(x, mean = effect_size, sd = se)
)

beta <- pnorm(crit, mean = effect_size, sd = se) -
        pnorm(-crit, mean = effect_size, sd = se)

power <- 1 - beta

ggplot() +
  # Type I error: two tails under the null distribution
  geom_area(
    data = subset(null, x <= -crit),
    aes(x = x, y = y, fill = "Type I Error (alpha)"),
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_area(
    data = subset(null, x >= crit),
    aes(x = x, y = y, fill = "Type I Error (alpha)"),
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  # Type II error: central region under the alternative distribution
  geom_area(
    data = subset(alternative, x >= -crit & x <= crit),
    aes(x = x, y = y, fill = "Type II Error (beta)"),
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  # Power: two tails under the alternative distribution
  geom_area(
    data = subset(alternative, x <= -crit),
    aes(x = x, y = y, fill = "Power"),
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_area(
    data = subset(alternative, x >= crit),
    aes(x = x, y = y, fill = "Power"),
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  # Null and alternative distributions
  geom_line(
    data = null,
    aes(x = x, y = y, color = "Null Distribution"),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = alternative,
    aes(x = x, y = y, color = "Alternative Distribution"),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  # Critical values
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = c(-crit, crit),
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "black"
  ) +
  # Type I error labels
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = -4.8, y = 0.025,
    label = "alpha/2",
    parse = TRUE,
    size = 4
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 4.5, y = 0.025,
    label = "alpha/2",
    parse = TRUE,
    size = 4
  ) +
  # Type II error label
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 0, y = 0.035,
    label = paste0("beta = ", round(beta, 2)),
    color = "darkorange3",
    size = 4
  ) +
  # Power label
  #annotate(
   # "text",
    #x = 7.5, y = 0.04,
    #label = paste0("Power = ", round(power, 2)),
    #color = "darkgreen",
    #size = 4
  #) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Error Regions",
    values = c(
      "Type I Error (alpha)" = "steelblue",
      "Type II Error (beta)" = "orange",
      "Power" = "darkgreen"
    )
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Sampling Distributions",
    values = c(
      "Null Distribution" = "steelblue4",
      "Alternative Distribution" = "darkgreen"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Sampling Distributions of the Difference in Means",
    subtitle = "Two-sided test with alpha = 0.05 and a true difference of 5 minutes",
    x = "Difference in Sample Means (minutes)",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-6, 11)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Power 

Power = 1 - P(Type II Error)! 

# Questions 

# Summary 

## Type I Error 

$\alpha = 0.05$ 

Probability of rejecting  $\mu_b = \mu_{bk}$ when  $\mu_b = \mu_{bk}$ is actually true.

```{r}

#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(ggplot2)

alpha <- 0.05
effect_size <- 5
se <- 1.852

crit <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2) * se

null <- data.frame(

)

# -------------------------
```

## Type II Error 

Probability of failing to reject  $\mu_b = \mu_{bk}$ when  $\mu_b = \mu_{bk}$ is actually false!


```{r}

# Type II Error

ggplot() +
  geom_area(
    data = subset(alternative, x >= -crit & x <= crit),

    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = null,
    aes(x = x, y = y),

    linetype = "dashed"
```

```{r}
    aes(x = x, y = y, fill = "Power"),
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  # Null and alternative distributions
  geom_line(
    data = null,
    aes(x = x, y = y, color = "Null Distribution"),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = alternative,
    aes(x = x, y = y, color = "Alternative Distribution"),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  # Critical values
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = c(-crit, crit),
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "black"
  ) +
  # Type I error labels
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = -4.8, y = 0.025,
    label = "alpha/2",
    parse = TRUE,
    size = 4
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 4.5, y = 0.025,
    label = "alpha/2",
    parse = TRUE,
    size = 4
  ) +
  # Type II error label
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 0, y = 0.035,
    label = paste0("beta = ", round(beta, 2)),
    color = "darkorange3",
    size = 4
  ) +
  # Power label
  #annotate(
   # "text",
    #x = 7.5, y = 0.04,
    #label = paste0("Power = ", round(power, 2)),
    #color = "darkgreen",
    #size = 4
  #) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Error Regions",
    values = c(
      "Type I Error (alpha)" = "steelblue",
      "Type II Error (beta)" = "orange",
      "Power" = "darkgreen"
    )
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Sampling Distributions",
    values = c(
      "Null Distribution" = "steelblue4",
      "Alternative Distribution" = "darkgreen"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Sampling Distributions of the Difference in Means",
    subtitle = "Two-sided test with alpha = 0.05 and a true difference of 5 minutes",
    x = "Difference in Sample Means (minutes)",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-6, 11)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

alpha <- 0.05
effect_size <- 10
se <- 1.852

crit <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2) * se

x <- seq(-6, 16, length.out = 2000)

null <- data.frame(
  x = x,
  y = dnorm(x, mean = 0, sd = se)
)

alternative <- data.frame(
  x = x,
  y = dnorm(x, mean = effect_size, sd = se)
)

beta <- pnorm(crit, mean = effect_size, sd = se) -
        pnorm(-crit, mean = effect_size, sd = se)

power <- 1 - beta

ggplot() +
  # Type I error: two tails under the null distribution
  geom_area(
    data = subset(null, x <= -crit),
    aes(x = x, y = y, fill = "Type I Error (alpha)"),
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_area(

    aes(x = x, y = y, fill = "Type I Error (alpha)"),
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  # Type II error: central region under the alternative distribution
  geom_area(
    data = subset(alternative, x >= -crit & x <= crit),

    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
```

## Changing α

When it's easier to reject, we reject more often... so power increases!

When it's easier to reject, we reject more often... when we shouldn't...

## In Summary{.smaller} 

| Change                   | Type I Error ($\alpha$) | Type II Error ($\beta$) | Power ($1-\beta$) |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------- | ----------------------- | ----------------- |
| **Increase sample size** | ↔️ No change            | ↓ Decreases             | ↑ Increases       |
| **Decrease sample size** | ↔️ No change            | ↑ Increases             | ↓ Decreases       |
| **Increase effect size** | ↔️ No change            | ↓ Decreases             | ↑ Increases       |
| **Decrease effect size** | ↔️ No change            | ↑ Increases             | ↓ Decreases       |
| **Increase $\alpha$**    | ↑ Increases             | ↓ Decreases             | ↑ Increases       |
| **Decrease $\alpha$**    | ↓ Decreases             | ↑ Increases             | ↓ Decreases       |

## Motivation 

We are going to study penguins! This real dataset includes measurements for penguin species, island in Palmer Archipelago, size (flipper length, body mass, bill dimensions), and sex. 


## Penguins{.smaller}

Suppose that we want to look at the relationship between sex and species. That is, we want to test if species of penguin is independent from sex. How is this different than what we’ve done before?

```{r}
penguins |>
  na.omit() |>
  group_by(species, sex) |>
  count()
```

## Chi-Square test 

The big picture idea is to compare expected counts (under the assumption of the null hypothesis with observed counts. This is how we are going to calculate our test statistic.

And we will start with this next week!
